tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תפלת אחר הקמת המצבה, מנהג ק״ק פרעסבורג יצ״ו
Prayer after the Unveiling of a Tombstone, according to the custom of the Jewish community of Pressburg

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer after the Unveiling of a Tombstone, according to the custom of the Jewish community of Pressburg

tei:lg.tei:l: according to the custom of the holy community of the Jews of Pressburg, yts”v]
May it be your will, elo’ah of all souls,
to mercifully account for the soul of _____,
upon whose burial spot we have erected a standing-monument.
This cairn is a witness.
Let its testimony be
that their memory never be forgotten
and their name never erased from Yisrael.
And this stone, that I have set as standing-monument,
shall be upon this house-of-hiding
for eternal remembrance.
Let it be, as the years pile up;
when children shall ask;
“What does this one indicate, this construction of rock?”;
let the elders of the city say,
“It is a burial place of a Yisrael.”
So let them leave it be for a full resting;
allow none to trouble their bones;
let Peace come to rest upon its sleeping-place.
Once more these bones shall live;
and be directed from the hiding-place;
[to travel] “from Naḥaliel/God’s Bequest to Bamot/Elevation.”
“And you, YHVH [Breath of Life, are enthroned] forever,
sitting throughout all generations”;
Revive us in your faithfulness;
and “by your light we will see light”
Then all of us can walk,
with your Name,
toward Right Living and Peace,
Amen, Selah.

tei:note.tei:p: יִשְׁמְרֵיהוּ צוּרוֹ וִיחַיֵּהוּ “May their Rock keep them and grant them life.” Kehilat Ḳodesh Pressburg, a/k/a Pozsony/Bratislava, the capital of Slovakia
matzeva means lit a standing rock, from n.tz.v, to stand in place
After Ezekiel 37:3, R’ David Evan Markus things this may also be a reference to the bones of Yaakov, hidden away until the Exodus. (See following note.)

from Naḥaliel to Bamot – Cf. Numbers 21:19 – part of the 42-stop journey of the Camp of the Israelites in their journey through the wilderness. “God’s resting/hiding place,” by this understanding, maps to the stop just prior to Naḥaliel, which was Matanah (lit., “Gift”). –David Evan Markus
Eichah 5:19, note the dichotomy of sitting forever vs. standing-monument forever
